interface.name: p_opentrons_TCG2_lid_interface_draft_v1
interface.description: Draft model-bound planning interface for Opentrons Thermocycler Module GEN2. Not executable control logic. Recipes and guards require separate evidence and review.

fibers.description: Local abstraction for a reported open lid. This draft does not infer temperature or sample readiness.

directions.description: Request lid closure after local checks.
Disable both temperature controllers; this does not assert immediate cooling.

fibers.description: Local abstraction for a reported closed lid. No target temperature, PCR profile or readiness is implied.

directions.description: Plan lid opening only after separately reviewed thermal and access checks.
Plan a target within the documented range; lowering a target relies on passive cooling.
Plan a separately specified block profile; repetitions and holds are not fixed in this interface.
Disable both temperature controllers; this does not assert immediate cooling.

entries.claim: GEN2 is model TCG2. Its block supports 4–99 °C and its lid supports 37–110 °C.
The lid supports open_lid() and close_lid(); these motion commands block other protocol steps.
Lowering a lid target permits passive cooling; the lid has no active cooling.
Profiles repeat a supplied sequence of block temperatures and holds. Lid temperature is configured separately.
deactivate() disables the block controller and lid heater.
The lid_position property can report open, closed, in_between or unknown.
Return the sample block to idle temperature before opening and removing samples. The lid seal may remain hot.

source.title: Thermocycler GEN2 Instruction Manual: Safety and Compliance

entries.claim: An idle white indicator does not establish that the module has cooled.
Two lid positions are a local planning abstraction. Intermediate and unknown readings, operational guards, recipes, temperatures, timing, concurrency and error recovery remain outside this draft.
This draft lists selected interface directions per position. It neither exhaustively admits hardware commands nor authorizes execution.
